 Australia pick two debutants for series-opening T20 International against England
 Jake Fraser-McGurk will make his international comeback in his native Melbourne alongside dual Aussie debutants and will partner captain Mitch Marsh at the top of the order in tonight’s first T20I.
 Marsh opted to bowl after winning the toss at the MCG against an England side ranked No.1 in the world that is on a seven-game winning streak in the shortest format.
 Hometown debutant Sam Harper will bat at No.3 and take the gloves with rising NSW and Sydney Sixers talent Lachlan Shaw to play as a specialist batter in his own international bow.
 The pair are among six Aussie changes from the third T20 against Bangladesh in June, where Marsh’s side secured a 3-0 sweep in their most recent series.
 Australia XI: Mitch Marsh (c), Jake Fraser-McGurk, Sam Harper (wk), Nikhil Chaudhary, Tim David, Lachlan Shaw, Jack Edwards, Joel Davies, Ben Dwarshuis, Adam Zampa, Riley Meredith
 England XI: Phil Salt, Aneurin Donald, Harry Brook (c), Tom Banton, Jordan Cox (wk), Sam Curran, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Liam Dawson, Henry Crocombe, Adil Rashid
 England have named 25-year-old quick Henry Crocombe to debut while veteran leg-spinner Adil Rashid will play his first match of the tour after being overlooked during the ODI series. Liam Dawson has also been picked in a dual spin attack.
 Australia have a completely new pace attack from that previous match with Nathan Ellis (side) injured, Spencer Johnson managed and Aaron Hardie not selected for the series.
 Ben Dwarshuis and Riley Meredith, both late call-ups with Xavier Bartlett (left knee) and Mahli Beardman (left quad) also injured, are the two frontline quicks for the series opener with additional pace support to come from allrounder Jack Edwards.
 Marsh will also have plenty of spin overs to call on, with Adam Zampa returning from back spasms that ruled him out of Wednesday’s series-deciding ODI in Hobart, as well as allrounders Nikhil Chaudhary and Joel Davies.
 Marsh, Tim David, Chaudhary, Davies and Zampa are the survivors from Australia's last T20 match.
 Fraser-McGurk, meanwhile, will play his first international since July last year when he made a one-off appearance against West Indies.
 The dashing 24-year-old opener has bounced back from a memorable maiden IPL season two years ago to earn his Australian recall with a hot start to the domestic summer for South Australia.
 He is the leading run-scorer in the One-Day Cup so far this season with scores of 46no, 88, 3, 122 and 56 in five one-day matches at a season strike rate of 187.5. He also hit his only international half-century in Australia’s last T20I against England in 2024.
 Harper (cap No.119) also earns his maiden T20I cap on the back of a stunning resurgence for Victoria and Melbourne Stars over the past 18 months.
 Shaw (cap No.120), an Australia under-19 representative in 2022, has big wraps in NSW where he was named captain of their 50-over side for this season.
 Australia v England T20I Series 2026
 First T20I: November 21, MCG, 7:15pm AEDT 
 Second T20I: November 24, Gold Coast Stadium, 7:15pm AEDT 
 Third T20I: November 27, The Gabba, 7:15pm AEDT 
 Fourth T20I: November 29, SCG, 7:15pm AEDT 
 Fifth T20I: December 2, Manuka Oval, 7:15pm AEDT 
 Australia squad: Mitchell Marsh (c), Xavier Bartlett, Mahli Beardman, Nikhil Chaudhary, Tim David, Joel Davies, Ben Dwarshuis, Jack Edwards, Jake Fraser-McGurk, Sam Harper, Spencer Johnson, Riley Meredith, Mitch Owen, Lachlan Shaw, Henry Thornton, Adam Zampa
 England squad: Harry Brook (c), Tom Banton, James Coles, Jordan Cox, Henry Crocombe, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Aneurin Donald, Eddie Jack, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid, Thomas Rew, Phil Salt, Luke Wood.
